title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 38
paragraphs: He thus escaped through Croesus; but afterwards he ended his life leaving no son to succeed him, and passed on his rule and his possessions to Stesagoras, who was the son of Cimon, his brother on the mother's side. The people of the Chersonese still offer sacrifices to him after his death, as is customary for a founder, and hold a contest of horse-races and athletic exercises in his honor, in which none of the men of Lampsacus are allowed to compete. After this there was war with those of Lampsacus; and it happened to Stesagoras also that he died without leaving a son, having been struck on the head with an axe in the city hall by a man who pretended to be a deserter but proved himself in fact to be an enemy, and a rather hot-blooded one at that.
